dedupe_keys.name: map layer of dams and fish passes on estonian watercourses environmental board

description: The Estonian Environmental Board announced in June 2022 a map layer in the environmental portal's map application that shows the locations of dams built on Estonian watercourses and whether they have fish passes. Most of the nearly 1,800 dam sites on the layer were mapped in an inventory in 2012 and 2013; existing dams are shown with an orange square, a cross marks a missing fish pass, and destroyed or removed dams are shown in blue. The layer sits under the water section of the portal's data and map page, and the board asks the public to report dams whose state has changed. The board says that in the preceding 12 years fish passes were added or damming removed at no fewer than 120 dams. The Ministry of Climate's page on dams in Estonia gives context: over 1,000 dams are counted on Estonian rivers, about 75 percent are impassable for fish and about 40 percent significantly affect river ecology. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: the data is partly outdated because many dams have since decayed or been removed, and some dams are missing. Coverage is Estonia. It supports blue infrastructure and river restoration planning, and dam safety and flood studies on small rivers; related records are the EELIS Estonian nature information system and the AMBER European barrier atlas.
